body:
**Starts** once #117 is merged.

## Why

The coordinator is the agent the user talks to. It runs the planning conversation and calls the workers (technical spec 1). This issue adds it with only the trip brief and memory tools. Then its conduct, the trip brief it sets up, and its memory rules can be tried in the terminal, before the browser chat (#52) exists.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 1, 5.1, 5.2, and 10.
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 4.
- [Persistence design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/persistence.md), section 6.

## Open questions

- ~~How does the coordinator know the maximum trip length? Technical spec 5.2 puts the maximum daily driving in its instructions, but not the maximum trip length, and the `update_trip_brief` input descriptions give neither. So the coordinator learns the limit only when an update is refused, which costs a round trip. Example: the user asks for "about three weeks", and it sends 21 days. Raised in PR #44's fourth review.~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: the maximum is in both the instructions and the input descriptions, filled in from the settings when the app starts. See "Do".
- ~~Where does the started-trip rule for memory go? The `memory` server's instructions (PR #116) say: "Once the trip has started, its trip memory can't change, and user memory still can. When a change is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why." The first sentence is about what memory means, so it may belong with the memory rules in the coordinator's instructions (technical spec 5.2) instead. Tool design section 4 puts a rule that covers several tools in the server's instructions, so moving it would change that section too. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23, while reviewing PR #116.~~ Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: no MCP server sends instructions anymore. A rule that covers several tools goes in each agent's system prompt instead, and #117 makes that change. The started-trip sentence is dropped, so the model learns that rule from the error, as with the `trip` server. See #117's open questions, and "Do" below.
- ~~How can Joe see, in one place, everything the coordinator is told? The model reads its system prompt, each MCP server's instructions, and each tool's name, description, and input schema as one unit. Today they're spread over several files, such as `src/tools/memory-tools.ts`, `memory-input.schema.ts`, and `memory-server.ts`. The schemas are built from Zod, and some limits are filled in from `settings.json`. So comparing two versions, such as before and after a change an evaluation (#53) tests, means reading several diffs. Two ways to fix it:~~
  - ~~Keep all the text in one config file, such as YAML, that the code reads.~~
  - ~~Keep the code as it is, and add a test that writes what each agent sees, as an MCP client gets it, into one checked-in file per agent. The test fails when the file is out of date. Then a PR's diff of that one file is the change to what the model sees, with the JSON Schema and the limits as the model gets them. Claude Code's suggestion, since it needs no rewrite. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-23.~~

  Settled in chat on 2026-10-23: the second way, a test that checks a file per agent is up to date, with `npm run agent-views` to rewrite it. It's its own issue, #118, after this one. Server instructions are gone too (#117).

## Do

- Add the coordinator, with only the tools on the `trip` server (`src/tools/trip-server.ts`, PR #44) and the `memory` server (#47). Its instructions cover conduct, the trip brief items to establish, the memory rules, and comfortable driving hours (technical spec, section 5.2).
- Put these rules for the `trip` and `memory` tools in the coordinator's instructions, word for word. They were the servers' instructions until #117 removed them, and tool design section 4 now says they go in the system prompt:
  - "Every tool that changes the trip makes the whole change or none of it. If any part is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why. Each of these tools replies with the feasibility check results the change made new or gone, anywhere in the trip."
  - "When a memory change is refused, nothing is changed, and the error says why."
- Give each trip brief item in the coordinator's instructions by the name the tools use, such as `tripLengthInDays`, with what it means (tool design, section 4). The `update_trip_brief` input descriptions say only how to pass each value, so the meanings are in no tool. Functional spec 5.2 gives most of them. It doesn't give these, which the input descriptions said before PR #44 trimmed them:
  - Interests and must-sees are in the user's words, with why they matter. A must-see can be one place, an area, a road, or an activity.
  - The rest days item records what the user asked for. It doesn't mark any day.
  - The default tier is the budget tier for lodging and meals when no budget rule covers them.
- Add a `coordinatorModel` setting to `settings.json`, set to the exact model ID `claude-opus-5-5`, and give it to the Agent SDK. A short name such as "opus" would move to newer models on its own, so a later run could use a different model. Write the setting into technical spec section 10. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-18.
- Give the coordinator the maximum trip length (functional spec 5.2). Add a trip length bullet next to comfortable driving hours in its instructions (technical spec 5.2): it gives the maximum, and says that when the user asks for more, explain the limit and propose a version that fits. Also give the limits in the `update_trip_brief` input descriptions: `tripLengthInDays` gets "from 1 to" the maximum trip length, and `comfortableDrivingInHours` gets "at most" the maximum daily driving. Fill in every number, in the instructions and the descriptions, from `settings.json` when the app starts, as the memory tools do for the item length. Never write a number into the text, so a changed setting can't leave stale text. Write this into technical spec 5.2 and 10, and tool design section 4. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-23.
- Add today's date to user messages, and the line after a resume, as technical spec section 5.2 says.
- Log each `mirror_error` message, with the session's ID and the error, and do nothing more. The Agent SDK sends the app that message when it drops transcript lines after 3 failed tries to save them (persistence design section 6). A few transcript lines out of order after a retry are accepted. Write both into persistence design section 6. Agreed in chat on 2026-10-18.
- Add a dev script to chat with the coordinator in the terminal, against the local database.

## Done when

Joe runs these conversations by hand in the terminal. Claude Code runs each one first, to catch problems before Joe's run, and the PR quotes the lines that show it.

- A discovery conversation fills in the trip brief, and `read_trip_brief` shows every item.
- "We never eat at chains" goes to user memory, and "skip I-35 this time" goes to trip memory.
- On a second trip, the coordinator confirms the user's usual driving hours instead of asking from scratch (functional spec 11, S9).
- Asked for 14 hours of driving a day, the coordinator pushes back, and sets no more than the maximum daily driving (technical spec section 10).

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from phase 13c of the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md).
